docs.title: Home
docs.text:
TorchStructure

TorchStructure is a python package for graph-based autodifferentiable structural design and engineering built upon PyTorch and Pytorch Geometric. To get started, you may want to take a look at the Installation Guide and Tutorials.

Early development

TorchStructure is in an early stage of development. It may contain bugs and will likely undergo API breaking changes.

  • Installation

  • Tutorials

  • API Reference

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text: Welcome to the installation guide for torch_structure. To ensure a smooth installation process, please follow the steps below.

docs.title: 1. (Optional, Recommended) Create a Virtual Environment
docs.text:
To avoid conflicts with other Python packages and to maintain a clean working environment, we highly recommend creating a new Python virtual environment.

For instance, with conda: 

conda create -n torch_structure_env python=3.12
conda activate torch_structure_env
conda install pip

or, with uv: 

uv venv --python 3.12

docs.title: 2. Install PyTorch
docs.text:
Visit the PyTorch Installation Guide to find the correct command for your system. We recommend installing the latest stable version.

For example, if using CUDA 12.8:

pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128

Warning

PyTorch requires a specific build depending on your system (e.g., CUDA version if you have a GPU). As a result, it cannot be automatically installed as part of the package dependencies and must be installed manually. All other dependencies, including PyTorch Geometric, are installed automatically.

docs.title: 3. Install torch_structure
docs.text:
Install the torch_structure package via pip:

pip install torch_structure

Alternative: Install directly from GitHub

To install the very latest version of torch_structure, clone the GitHub repository:

git clone https://github.com/lazlo-bleker/torch-structure.git

Followed by creating an editable installation using the following command from within the cloned repository:

pip install -e .

Optional: PyTorch Geometric extensions

torch_structure does not require the compiled PyTorch Geometric extensions (torch_scatter, pyg_lib, ...). If they are installed, PyTorch Geometric uses them automatically where they are faster. See the PyTorch Geometric Installation Guide for how to install them.

docs.title: 4. Verify the Installation
docs.text:
To verify the installation, open Python and run the following:

import torch_structure as ts

If no errors occur you have succesfully installed torch_structure.

docs.title: edge_direction(edge_index, x, return_length=False)
docs.text:
Compute the unit vector (and optionally the length) along each edge.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default edge_index Tensor[2, E]

edge connectivity.

required x Tensor[N, D]

node coordinates.

required return_length bool

if True, also return each edge's length.

False

Returns:

Type Description

torch.Tensor [E, D] or tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: the

normalized direction from source to target node, and, if

return_length is True, a [E, 1] tensor of edge lengths.

Source code in src/torch_structure/utils.py 
def edge_direction(edge_index, x, return_length=False):
    """Compute the unit vector (and optionally the length) along each edge.

    Args:
        edge_index (torch.Tensor [2, E]): edge connectivity.
        x (torch.Tensor [N, D]): node coordinates.
        return_length (bool): if ``True``, also return each edge's length.

    Returns:
        torch.Tensor [E, D] or tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: the
        normalized direction from source to target node, and, if
        ``return_length`` is ``True``, a ``[E, 1]`` tensor of edge lengths.
    """
    row, col = edge_index
    direction = x[col] - x[row]
    length = torch.norm(direction, dim=1, keepdim=True)
    normalized_direction = direction / (length + 1e-9)

    if return_length:
        return normalized_direction, length
    else:
        return normalized_direction

def effective_stiffness(edge_index, E, A, length):
    """Compute effective stiffness."""
    stiffness = E * A / length
    aggregator = StiffnessAggregator()
    K_eff = aggregator(edge_index, stiffness)
    return K_eff

docs.title: scipy_jacobian(func)
docs.text:
Wrap a scalar-valued torch function for use with scipy's gradient-based optimizers.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default func Callable[..., Tensor]

differentiable function that takes a 1D torch tensor (plus optional extra args) and returns a scalar loss.

required

Returns:

Type Description

Callable[[numpy.ndarray, ...], tuple[float, numpy.ndarray]]: a

function taking a numpy array (plus the same extra args) that

returns the (loss, gradient) pair expected by

scipy.optimize.minimize(jac=True). The returned function tracks

the best loss seen so far in its best_loss attribute.

Source code in src/torch_structure/utils.py 
def scipy_jacobian(func):
    """Wrap a scalar-valued torch function for use with scipy's gradient-based optimizers.

    Args:
        func (Callable[..., torch.Tensor]): differentiable function that
            takes a 1D torch tensor (plus optional extra args) and returns a
            scalar loss.

    Returns:
        Callable[[numpy.ndarray, ...], tuple[float, numpy.ndarray]]: a
        function taking a numpy array (plus the same extra args) that
        returns the ``(loss, gradient)`` pair expected by
        ``scipy.optimize.minimize(jac=True)``. The returned function tracks
        the best loss seen so far in its ``best_loss`` attribute.
    """
    # TODO: drop best_loss once Python 3.9/3.10 (Rhino 8) support is dropped and scipy>=1.17 can be
    # required; from 1.17 SLSQP passes callbacks the iterate itself (callback(intermediate_result) with
    # .x and .fun). best_loss is the lowest loss of any evaluation, including trial points, so it can
    # differ from the current iterate's loss.
    func_grad_and_value = torch.func.grad_and_value(func)

    def func_scipy(x_np, *args):
        """Evaluate ``func`` and its gradient at ``x_np``, tracking the best loss seen."""
        x = torch.tensor(x_np, dtype=torch.float64)
        grad_val, loss_val = func_grad_and_value(x, *args)
        loss, grad = loss_val.item(), grad_val.detach().numpy()
        func_scipy.best_loss = min(loss, func_scipy.best_loss)
        return loss, grad

    func_scipy.best_loss = np.inf
    return func_scipy

docs.title: transformation_matrix(edge_index, x, length)
docs.text:
Create a 3D tensor containing the transformation matrices for all edges in a 3D truss.

Parameters: - edge_index: Tensor of shape [2, num_edges], containing indices of connected nodes for each edge. - x: Tensor of shape [num_nodes, 3], containing the coordinates (x, y, z) of each node. - length: Tensor of shape [num_edges], containing the length of each edge.

Returns: - matrix: Tensor of shape [num_edges, 2, 6], containing the transformation matrices for all edges.

Source code in src/torch_structure/utils.py 
def transformation_matrix(edge_index, x, length):
    """
    Create a 3D tensor containing the transformation matrices for all edges in a 3D truss.

    Parameters:
    - edge_index: Tensor of shape [2, num_edges], containing indices of connected nodes for each edge.
    - x: Tensor of shape [num_nodes, 3], containing the coordinates (x, y, z) of each node.
    - length: Tensor of shape [num_edges], containing the length of each edge.

    Returns:
    - matrix: Tensor of shape [num_edges, 2, 6], containing the transformation matrices for all edges.
    """
    # Extract coordinates of nodes connected by edges
    coords_i = x[edge_index[0]]  # Shape: [num_edges, 3]
    coords_j = x[edge_index[1]]  # Shape: [num_edges, 3]

    # Compute direction cosines (l, m, n)
    direction_vector = coords_j - coords_i  # Shape: [num_edges, 3]
    direction_cosines = direction_vector / length.view(-1, 1)  # Shape: [num_edges, 3]

    # Initialize the transformation matrix tensor
    T = torch.zeros(
        (edge_index.size(1), 2, 6), device=x.device
    )  # Shape: [num_edges, 2, 6]

    # Directly assign the direction cosines to the appropriate places
    T[:, 0, :3] = direction_cosines  # First row maps Node 1's global displacements
    T[:, 1, 3:] = direction_cosines  # Second row maps Node 2's global displacements

    return T

docs.title: condense_releases(k, release)
docs.text:
Apply member end releases to local stiffness matrices by static condensation.

Releasing torsion at either end removes the member's torsional stiffness. Released bending rotations are condensed out, so the member carries no moment about that axis at that end and the released DOFs' rows and columns become zero. Releasing every rotation at both ends turns the member into a pin-ended truss bar.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default k Tensor[E, 12, 12]

local stiffness matrices.

required release (Tensor[E, 6], bool)

released rotations, ordered [rx_i, ry_i, rz_i, rx_j, ry_j, rz_j] in local member axes.

required

Returns:

Type Description

torch.Tensor [E, 12, 12]: condensed local stiffness matrices.

Source code in src/torch_structure/analysis/elements.py 
def condense_releases(k, release):
    """Apply member end releases to local stiffness matrices by static condensation.

    Releasing torsion at either end removes the member's torsional stiffness. Released bending
    rotations are condensed out, so the member carries no moment about that axis at that end and
    the released DOFs' rows and columns become zero. Releasing every rotation at both ends turns
    the member into a pin-ended truss bar.

    Args:
        k (torch.Tensor [E, 12, 12]): local stiffness matrices.
        release (torch.Tensor [E, 6], bool): released rotations, ordered
            ``[rx_i, ry_i, rz_i, rx_j, ry_j, rz_j]`` in local member axes.

    Returns:
        torch.Tensor [E, 12, 12]: condensed local stiffness matrices.
    """
    release = release.view(-1, 6).to(torch.bool)

    # torsion: a torsion-released member carries no torque at all
    no_torsion = release[:, 0] | release[:, 3]
    keep = torch.ones(k.shape[0], 12, dtype=k.dtype, device=k.device)
    keep[:, 3] = torch.where(no_torsion, 0.0, 1.0).to(k.dtype)
    keep[:, 9] = keep[:, 3]
    k = k * keep.unsqueeze(2) * keep.unsqueeze(1)

    # bending: condense K_c = K - K M (M K M + I - M)^-1 M K, with M selecting released rotations.
    # The rotational bending block is positive definite, so the system is always invertible.
    M = torch.zeros(k.shape[0], 12, dtype=k.dtype, device=k.device)
    M[:, [4, 5, 10, 11]] = release[:, [1, 2, 4, 5]].to(k.dtype)
    if not M.any():
        return k

    M_left = M.unsqueeze(2)
    M_right = M.unsqueeze(1)
    # released DOFs without bending stiffness (e.g. Iz = 0) have zero rows; a unit diagonal keeps
    # the system solvable without coupling them to anything
    no_stiffness = (torch.diagonal(k, dim1=1, dim2=2) == 0).to(k.dtype) * M
    released_block = M_left * k * M_right + torch.diag_embed(1 - M + no_stiffness)
    X = torch.linalg.solve(released_block, M_left * k)
    k = k - k @ X

    # remove round-off left in the released rows and columns
    keep = 1 - M
    return k * keep.unsqueeze(2) * keep.unsqueeze(1)

docs.title: local_axes(coords_i, coords_j, roll=None, vertical_tol=1e-06)
docs.text:
Compute each member's length and local coordinate system.

The local x-axis runs from node i to node j. The local z-axis lies in the vertical plane containing the member and points upwards; for vertical members, where that plane is undefined, the local z-axis is global +X. The local y-axis completes the right-handed system. A roll angle then rotates the local y- and z-axes about the local x-axis.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default coords_i Tensor[E, 3]

coordinates of each member's start node.

required coords_j Tensor[E, 3]

coordinates of each member's end node.

required roll Tensor[E] or [E, 1]

rotation of the cross-section about the local x-axis, in radians. Default is no rotation.

None vertical_tol float

members whose direction is within this tolerance of global Z are treated as vertical.

1e-06

Returns:

Type Description

tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: member lengths [E] and rotation matrices

[E, 3, 3] whose rows are the local x-, y- and z-axes in global coordinates.

Source code in src/torch_structure/analysis/elements.py 
def local_axes(coords_i, coords_j, roll=None, vertical_tol=1e-6):
    """Compute each member's length and local coordinate system.

    The local x-axis runs from node i to node j. The local z-axis lies in the vertical plane
    containing the member and points upwards; for vertical members, where that plane is
    undefined, the local z-axis is global +X. The local y-axis completes the right-handed
    system. A ``roll`` angle then rotates the local y- and z-axes about the local x-axis.

    Args:
        coords_i (torch.Tensor [E, 3]): coordinates of each member's start node.
        coords_j (torch.Tensor [E, 3]): coordinates of each member's end node.
        roll (torch.Tensor [E] or [E, 1], optional): rotation of the cross-section about the
            local x-axis, in radians. Default is no rotation.
        vertical_tol (float): members whose direction is within this tolerance of global Z are
            treated as vertical.

    Returns:
        tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: member lengths ``[E]`` and rotation matrices
        ``[E, 3, 3]`` whose rows are the local x-, y- and z-axes in global coordinates.
    """
    delta = coords_j - coords_i
    length = torch.linalg.norm(delta, dim=1)
    x = delta / length.unsqueeze(1)

    global_z = torch.tensor([0.0, 0.0, 1.0], dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device).expand_as(x)
    global_x = torch.tensor([1.0, 0.0, 0.0], dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device).expand_as(x)
    is_vertical = (x[:, 2].abs() > 1 - vertical_tol).unsqueeze(1)
    reference = torch.where(is_vertical, global_x, global_z)

    y = torch.linalg.cross(reference, x)
    y = y / torch.linalg.norm(y, dim=1, keepdim=True)
    z = torch.linalg.cross(x, y)

    if roll is not None:
        roll = roll.view(-1, 1).to(x.dtype)
        cos, sin = torch.cos(roll), torch.sin(roll)
        y, z = cos * y + sin * z, -sin * y + cos * z

    return length, torch.stack([x, y, z], dim=1)

docs.title: local_stiffness(length, E, A, Iy, Iz, J, G)
docs.text:
Assemble the 12x12 Euler-Bernoulli frame stiffness matrix of each member in local coordinates.

The DOFs per node are ordered [ux, uy, uz, rx, ry, rz], node i first. Bending about the local z-axis (displacement in local y) uses Iz, and bending about the local y-axis (displacement in local z) uses Iy. A member with Iy = Iz = J = 0 is a truss bar.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default length Tensor[E]

member lengths.

required E Tensor[E]

Young's moduli.

required A Tensor[E]

cross-sectional areas.

required Iy Tensor[E]

second moments of area about the local y-axis.

required Iz Tensor[E]

second moments of area about the local z-axis.

required J Tensor[E]

torsion constants.

required G Tensor[E]

shear moduli.

required

Returns:

Type Description

torch.Tensor [E, 12, 12]: local stiffness matrices.

Source code in src/torch_structure/analysis/elements.py 
def local_stiffness(length, E, A, Iy, Iz, J, G):
    """Assemble the 12x12 Euler-Bernoulli frame stiffness matrix of each member in local coordinates.

    The DOFs per node are ordered ``[ux, uy, uz, rx, ry, rz]``, node i first. Bending about the
    local z-axis (displacement in local y) uses ``Iz``, and bending about the local y-axis
    (displacement in local z) uses ``Iy``. A member with ``Iy = Iz = J = 0`` is a truss bar.

    Args:
        length (torch.Tensor [E]): member lengths.
        E (torch.Tensor [E]): Young's moduli.
        A (torch.Tensor [E]): cross-sectional areas.
        Iy (torch.Tensor [E]): second moments of area about the local y-axis.
        Iz (torch.Tensor [E]): second moments of area about the local z-axis.
        J (torch.Tensor [E]): torsion constants.
        G (torch.Tensor [E]): shear moduli.

    Returns:
        torch.Tensor [E, 12, 12]: local stiffness matrices.
    """
    L = length
    k = torch.zeros(L.shape[0], 12, 12, dtype=L.dtype, device=L.device)

    def add(dofs, coefficients):
        # scatter a 2x2 or 4x4 block of per-member coefficients into k
        for a, row in enumerate(dofs):
            for b, col in enumerate(dofs):
                k[:, row, col] = k[:, row, col] + coefficients[a][b]

    axial = E * A / L
    add((0, 6), [[axial, -axial], [-axial, axial]])

    torsion = G * J / L
    add((3, 9), [[torsion, -torsion], [-torsion, torsion]])

    # bending in the local x-y plane: displacement uy, rotation rz
    c = E * Iz / L**3
    add(
        (1, 5, 7, 11),
        [
            [12 * c, 6 * L * c, -12 * c, 6 * L * c],
            [6 * L * c, 4 * L**2 * c, -6 * L * c, 2 * L**2 * c],
            [-12 * c, -6 * L * c, 12 * c, -6 * L * c],
            [6 * L * c, 2 * L**2 * c, -6 * L * c, 4 * L**2 * c],
        ],
    )

    # bending in the local x-z plane: displacement uz, rotation ry (opposite rotation sign)
    c = E * Iy / L**3
    add(
        (2, 4, 8, 10),
        [
            [12 * c, -6 * L * c, -12 * c, -6 * L * c],
            [-6 * L * c, 4 * L**2 * c, 6 * L * c, 2 * L**2 * c],
            [-12 * c, 6 * L * c, 12 * c, 6 * L * c],
            [-6 * L * c, 2 * L**2 * c, 6 * L * c, 4 * L**2 * c],
        ],
    )

    return k

docs.title: transformation_matrix(rotation)
docs.text:
Expand per-member 3x3 rotation matrices to the 12x12 member transformation matrix.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rotation Tensor[E, 3, 3]

rotation matrices from local_axes.

required

Returns:

Type Description

torch.Tensor [E, 12, 12]: block-diagonal matrices mapping global to local member DOFs.

Source code in src/torch_structure/analysis/elements.py 
def transformation_matrix(rotation):
    """Expand per-member 3x3 rotation matrices to the 12x12 member transformation matrix.

    Args:
        rotation (torch.Tensor [E, 3, 3]): rotation matrices from
            [local_axes][torch_structure.analysis.elements.local_axes].

    Returns:
        torch.Tensor [E, 12, 12]: block-diagonal matrices mapping global to local member DOFs.
    """
    num_members = rotation.shape[0]
    T = torch.zeros(num_members, 12, 12, dtype=rotation.dtype, device=rotation.device)
    for k in range(4):
        T[:, 3 * k : 3 * k + 3, 3 * k : 3 * k + 3] = rotation
    return T

docs.title: frame_analysis(coords, edge_index, load, support_dofs, E, A, Iy=None, Iz=None, J=None, G=None, roll=None, release=None, moment=None, batch=None, dtype=torch.float64, null_tol=1e-09)
docs.text:
Performs a linear-elastic analysis of a 3D frame of Euler-Bernoulli members, which may be mixed with pin-ended truss bars.

Every node has six DOFs [ux, uy, uz, rx, ry, rz]. A member carries axial force, torsion and bending, minus whatever its release frees: releasing every rotation at both ends gives a pin-ended truss bar, as does leaving Iy, Iz and J at zero. Nodal rotations that no member restrains, such as at the joints of a pure truss, are fixed automatically, so trusses need no rotational supports.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default coords Tensor

A tensor of shape (num_nodes, 3) containing the coordinates of each node.

required edge_index Tensor

A tensor of shape (2, num_members) with the start and end node of each member.

required load Tensor

A tensor of shape (num_nodes, 3) containing the nodal forces.

required support_dofs Tensor

A boolean tensor of shape (num_nodes, 6) marking restrained DOFs [ux, uy, uz, rx, ry, rz], e.g. StructData.support_dofs.

required E Tensor or float

Young's modulus per member, shape (num_members, 1).

required A Tensor or float

Cross-sectional area per member, shape (num_members, 1).

required Iy Tensor or float

Second moment of area about the local y-axis per member. Default is 0.

None Iz Tensor or float

Second moment of area about the local z-axis per member. Default is 0.

None J Tensor or float

Torsion constant per member. Default is 0.

None G Tensor or float

Shear modulus per member. Default is E / 2.6 (Poisson's ratio 0.3).

None roll Tensor or float

def frame_analysis(
    coords,
    edge_index,
    load,
    support_dofs,
    E,
    A,
    Iy=None,
    Iz=None,
    J=None,
    G=None,
    roll=None,
    release=None,
    moment=None,
    batch=None,
    dtype=torch.float64,
    null_tol=1e-9,
):
    """
    Performs a linear-elastic analysis of a 3D frame of Euler-Bernoulli members, which may be
    mixed with pin-ended truss bars.

    Every node has six DOFs ``[ux, uy, uz, rx, ry, rz]``. A member carries axial force, torsion
    and bending, minus whatever its ``release`` frees: releasing every rotation at both ends
    gives a pin-ended truss bar, as does leaving ``Iy``, ``Iz`` and ``J`` at zero. Nodal rotations
    that no member restrains, such as at the joints of a pure truss, are fixed automatically, so
    trusses need no rotational supports.

    Args:
        coords (torch.Tensor): A tensor of shape (num_nodes, 3) containing the coordinates of
            each node.
        edge_index (torch.Tensor): A tensor of shape (2, num_members) with the start and end node
            of each member.
        load (torch.Tensor): A tensor of shape (num_nodes, 3) containing the nodal forces.
        support_dofs (torch.Tensor): A boolean tensor of shape (num_nodes, 6) marking restrained DOFs
            ``[ux, uy, uz, rx, ry, rz]``, e.g.
            [StructData.support_dofs][torch_structure.data.data.StructData.support_dofs].
        E (torch.Tensor or float): Young's modulus per member, shape (num_members, 1).
        A (torch.Tensor or float): Cross-sectional area per member, shape (num_members, 1).
        Iy (torch.Tensor or float, optional): Second moment of area about the local y-axis per
            member. Default is 0.
        Iz (torch.Tensor or float, optional): Second moment of area about the local z-axis per
            member. Default is 0.
        J (torch.Tensor or float, optional): Torsion constant per member. Default is 0.
        G (torch.Tensor or float, optional): Shear modulus per member. Default is ``E / 2.6``
            (Poisson's ratio 0.3).
        roll (torch.Tensor or float, optional): Rotation of each member's cross-section about its
            axis, in radians. See
            [local_axes][torch_structure.analysis.elements.local_axes]. Default is 0.
        release (torch.Tensor, optional): A boolean tensor of shape (num_members, 6) marking
            released end rotations ``[rx_i, ry_i, rz_i, rx_j, ry_j, rz_j]`` in local member axes.
            Default is no releases (rigid joints).
        moment (torch.Tensor, optional): A tensor of shape (num_nodes, 3) containing nodal
            moments about the global axes. Default is no moments.
        batch (torch.Tensor, optional): A tensor of shape (num_nodes,) assigning each node to a
            graph. Default is a single graph.
        dtype (torch.dtype, optional): Precision of the assembly and solve. Results are cast back
            to the dtype of ``coords``. Default is ``torch.float64``.
        null_tol (float, optional): Relative tolerance below which a nodal rotation counts as
            unrestrained by any member. Default is 1e-9.

    Returns:
        FrameResult: A named tuple of ``displacement``, ``rotation``, ``force``, ``end_forces``,
        ``reaction_force`` and ``reaction_moment``; see [FrameResult][torch_structure.analysis.frame.FrameResult].
    """
    out_dtype = coords.dtype
    device = coords.device
    num_nodes = coords.shape[0]
    num_members = edge_index.shape[1]
    src, dst = edge_index[0], edge_index[1]

    def member_attr(value, default):
        if value is None:
            value = default
        value = torch.as_tensor(value, device=device).to(dtype)
        return value.expand(num_members) if value.numel() == 1 else value.reshape(-1)

    E = member_attr(E, None)
    A = member_attr(A, None)
    Iy = member_attr(Iy, 0.0)
    Iz = member_attr(Iz, 0.0)
    J = member_attr(J, 0.0)
    G = member_attr(G, E / 2.6)
    roll = None if roll is None else member_attr(roll, 0.0)

    # Member stiffness in global coordinates
    coords = coords.to(dtype)
    length, rotation = local_axes(coords[src], coords[dst], roll)
    k_local = local_stiffness(length, E, A, Iy, Iz, J, G)
    if release is not None:
        k_local = condense_releases(k_local, release)
    T = transformation_matrix(rotation)
    k_global = T.transpose(1, 2) @ k_local @ T

    # DOF numbering, padded per graph
    if batch is None:
        batch = torch.zeros(num_nodes, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    batch = batch.view(-1)
    num_graphs = int(batch.max().item()) + 1
    counts = torch.bincount(batch, minlength=num_graphs)
    local_node = torch.arange(num_nodes, device=device) - (torch.cumsum(counts, 0) - counts)[batch]
    num_dofs = 6 * int(counts.max().item())

    node_dof = 6 * local_node.unsqueeze(1) + torch.arange(6, device=device)  # [N, 6]
    node_flat = batch.unsqueeze(1) * num_dofs + node_dof  # [N, 6] into [G * num_dofs]

    # Assembly
    member_dof = torch.cat([node_dof[src], node_dof[dst]], dim=1)  # [E, 12]
    member_offset = (batch[src] * num_dofs * num_dofs).view(-1, 1, 1)
    member_flat = member_offset + member_dof.unsqueeze(2) * num_dofs + member_dof.unsqueeze(1)
    K = torch.zeros(num_graphs * num_dofs * num_dofs, dtype=dtype, device=device)
    K = K.index_add(0, member_flat.reshape(-1), k_global.reshape(-1))
    K = K.view(num_graphs, num_dofs, num_dofs)

    if moment is None:
        moment = torch.zeros_like(load)
    nodal_load = torch.cat([load, moment], dim=1).to(dtype)
    F = torch.zeros(num_graphs * num_dofs, dtype=dtype, device=device)
    F = F.index_add(0, node_flat.reshape(-1), nodal_load.reshape(-1)).view(num_graphs, num_dofs)

    # Restrained DOFs, including padding, are removed by a unit-scaled diagonal
    support_dofs = support_dofs.to(device=device, dtype=torch.bool)
    if support_dofs.shape != (num_nodes, 6):
        raise ValueError(f"support_dofs must have shape ({num_nodes}, 6), but got {tuple(support_dofs.shape)}.")
    fixed = torch.ones(num_graphs * num_dofs, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
    fixed[node_flat.reshape(-1)] = support_dofs.reshape(-1)
    fixed = fixed.view(num_graphs, num_dofs)
    free = (~fixed).to(dtype)

    scale = torch.diagonal(K, dim1=1, dim2=2).detach().abs().amax(dim=1).clamp_min(1.0)
    K_reduced = K * free.unsqueeze(2) * free.unsqueeze(1) + torch.diag_embed(fixed * scale.view(-1, 1))
    F_reduced = F * free

    # Nodal rotations no member restrains are null directions of the stiffness matrix. A spring
    # along exactly these directions makes the system solvable without changing the solution.
    rot_flat = node_dof[:, 3:]
    rows = rot_flat.unsqueeze(2).expand(-1, 3, 3)
    cols = rot_flat.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, 3, 3)
    graph = batch.view(-1, 1, 1).expand(-1, 3, 3)
    with torch.no_grad():
        eigenvalues, eigenvectors = torch.linalg.eigh(K_reduced[graph, rows, cols])
        node_scale = scale[batch].view(-1, 1)
        is_null = (eigenvalues <= null_tol * node_scale).to(dtype)
        spring = eigenvectors @ torch.diag_embed(is_null * node_scale) @ eigenvectors.transpose(1, 2)
    K_reduced = K_reduced.index_put((graph, rows, cols), spring, accumulate=True)

    # Solve
    u = torch.linalg.solve(K_reduced, F_reduced.unsqueeze(2)).squeeze(2)
    u_nodes = u.reshape(-1)[node_flat]  # [N, 6]

    reaction = (K @ u.unsqueeze(2)).squeeze(2) - F
    reaction = reaction.reshape(-1)[node_flat] * support_dofs.to(dtype)

    # Member end forces in local axes
    u_members = torch.cat([u_nodes[src], u_nodes[dst]], dim=1).unsqueeze(2)
    end_forces = (k_local @ (T @ u_members)).squeeze(2)
    force = end_forces[:, 6:7]

    return FrameResult(
        displacement=u_nodes[:, :3].to(out_dtype),
        rotation=u_nodes[:, 3:].to(out_dtype),
        force=force.to(out_dtype),
        end_forces=end_forces.to(out_dtype),
        reaction_force=reaction[:, :3].to(out_dtype),
        reaction_moment=reaction[:, 3:].to(out_dtype),
    )

Bases: TSMixin, Data

A torch_geometric.data.Data subclass representing a directed, reciprocal-edge structural graph.

Every undirected edge is stored as a pair of opposite directed edges; directed_mask marks one edge of each pair as the "canonical" direction, and reciprocal_edge maps each edge to its opposite. This lets edge attributes be defined once per undirected edge (via edge_attr_to_undirected) while message passing still sees both directions. Node/edge/graph attributes are declared through node_attrs/edge_attrs/graph_attrs, and nodes carry a name attribute enabling NetworkX-style access via nodes and name-based editing methods such as add_edge.
